chunks: 1208 - What Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurarah, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked him about a man who leads a people in prayer for two rak'ahs, then informs them that he was not in a state of wudu (ablution).
He said: "The people complete their prayer, for there is no liability upon the Imam."

key_terms.الْقَوْمُ: the congregation or the people praying behind the Imam
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rak'ahs, two units of salat
key_terms.ضَمَانٌ: liability or responsibility in this legal context
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the ritual state of purity required for salat

ai.seo_question: What should a congregation do if the Imam realizes after leading them that he had no wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning congregational salat when the Imam later discovers or admits that he lacked wudu (ablution). The ruling is that the congregation completes its prayer, because liability for their prayer is not borne by the Imam in this case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1208 - Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (as) who said:
"I asked him about a man who leads a congregation for two rak'ahs and then informs them that he was not in a state of wudu' (ritual purity).
Imam (as) said: 'The congregation should complete their prayer because the Imam bears no responsibility (for their prayers).'".
